messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: - Medicines broken down by CYP2D6. Sertraline blocks this liver enzyme, so levels of these drugs can rise and doses may need to be lowered. Examples include propafenone, flecainide, atomoxetine, desipramine, dextromethorphan, metoprolol, nebivolol, perphenazine, thioridazine, tolterodine, and venlafaxine.
- Phenytoin and fosphenytoin. Sertraline can raise phenytoin levels, so levels should be checked when sertraline is started or the dose is changed.
- Medicines that prolong the QTc interval. These should generally be avoided. Examples include certain antipsychotics (ziprasidone, iloperidone, chlorpromazine, mesoridazine, droperidol), certain antibiotics (erythromycin, gatifloxacin, moxifloxacin, sparfloxacin), Class 1A antiarrhythmics (quinidine, procainamide), Class III antiarrhythmics (amiodarone, sotalol), and others including pentamidine, methadone, halofantrine, mefloquine, dolasetron, probucol, and tacrolimus.
- Disulfiram, with the oral solution only, because of its alcohol content.
Triplet: ["Sertraline", "increases plasma levels of", "dextromethorphan"]

The relation 'increases plasma levels of' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug increases the plasma levels of the drug specified by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'increases level of': The subject drug increases the level of the substance or biomarker specified by the object entity in the body.
B. 'increases effect of': The subject drug enhances or potentiates the effect of the substance or condition specified by the object entity.
C. 'metabolism': The subject drug is metabolized in the body in the manner specified by the object entity.
D. 'has higher blood levels in': The subject drug remains at higher concentrations in the blood of the group specified by the object entity.
E. 'has effect': The subject drug produces the therapeutic or physiological effect specified by the object entity.
F. None of the above.
